comment: Dr. Price LOVES books.  If you like to read, this is the class for you.  If you don't like reading, you can get by without doing the reading as long as you participate in the side discussions competently.

Dr. Price is great. Slightly-above-average difficulty class, but it's worthwhile. His classes do keep you on your toes, but it's an experience you'll 100% learn from and bond with your classmates over. He does a great job opening up the class to discussions, which are usually remarkably good. Accessible in office hours, too. Would recommend!

Such a caring and kind professor. Even if the course content is difficult and confusing, he is very patient and makes sure that everyone understands. He tries to get to know each student individually. Class is harder to follow if you don't keep up with the readings. Seminar style and cold calling, so it's obvious if you don't do the reading

I honestly loved Dr. Price. He was great at facilitating discussions and forcing students to ask hard questions about their beliefs and mindsets. You have to work for your grade, but he will go out of his way to help you get a good grade and understand the material.

Dr.Price is the best!!! This is definitely a hard class and he does not go easy on you. However, Price is the type of teacher you want to work hard for and do well. He is incredibly caring and is clearly knowledgeable on the subject. He does cold call but do not let that deter you! Has all his students over to his house for lunch each semester.

Dr. Price is an amazing professor. He does an excellent job teaching difficult material and wants you to do well. He provides good feedback and will help you improve in the course. He understands that most Jepson students are not particularly interested in philosophy or critical thinking and tailors courses and teaching to make it engaging.

Incredibly polarizing to students, and his didacticism is both his greatest gift and curse as an educator; instructor of critical thinking and ethics, he is also the sole conduit for almost all "discussion"/call-and-response. Despite how he may dispense with social tact, he will always go about 10 extra miles to help you succeed if you so desire.

Dr. Price is the type of professor that you want to do well for. He facilitates class discussion nicely. You must read and you must come to class which is a good thing. Other comments said he can be vague, which I get, sometimes I think he thinks too hard about how to make his assignments challenging and different. Probably my fav prof in Jepson.

I have loved both my Crit. Thinking and Ldsp. Ethics with Price. Maybe it depends on the makeup of students in the class, but my favorite part of both classes was the discussions. Price led them well and made them entertaining while ensuring that he clearly laid out what we needed to know. For my midterm in Ethics, he told us exactly what was on it

Very knowledgeable, but just not a good teacher.  Is very vague about everything so it doesn't look like he's taking a stand.  The '1' on the helpfulness (the lowest I've ever given in that category) comes from his completely illegible comments on papers and empty words when you come for help.

Had him for critical thinking, I dont know what the other commenters are thinking.  He is a good prof who teaches well, if you dont know the stuff before but read the book you will be fine.  I never brought the books and did well.  He does have weakly tests though, which are not hard if you review your notes before class.

Odd that such a socially awkward person has such a high opinion of his own ideas and is so judgmental of fields in which he has not served. Behaves as if born with knowledge and wisdom,and disparaging of those who won't accept his pronouncements at face value.
TPrice is pretty socially awkward. Dorky but cute. He is a difficult grader, but very willing to help you with assignments.
take the other professor....price has exams and they're hard. his class is torture to sit through.
